decisions.title: Architecture Drivers, Quality Attributes, Workload Assumptions & Trust Boundaries
decisions.rationale: Current semantic and experience authority requires trust/authority correctness to constrain lower-priority continuity and sustaining qualities; current evidence supports bounded bursty live-event workload, safe degraded/paper continuity, explicit trust boundaries, proportional complexity and evidence-bounded quantitative targets. Historical foundation material was revalidated as evidence but not adopted.
rejected_alternatives: Historical foundation unchanged — chronology cannot create authority.
Unranked qualities — insufficient tradeoff rule when continuity conflicts with authority/security.
Scale-first/distributed-first — no demonstrated workload driver for speculative distribution.
decisions.reversibility_migration: Low-cost foundational decision before downstream mechanisms are selected. Reopening after later ADQ acceptance requires revalidation of dependent decisions. No data or runtime migration is created by ADQ-001 itself.

decisions.title: Application Ownership, Decomposition & Dependency Topology
alternatives_evaluated: Historical six-module modular monolith after Q4 repair
decisions.rationale: Current semantic cohesion and Phase-019 drivers favor one authoritative modular application boundary with five cohesive modules. Combining historical Judging Operations and Evaluation reduces avoidable cross-module transaction/coordination pressure while preserving Concept boundaries. Selective distribution lacks a demonstrated scale/isolation/ownership driver, while a broad monolith insufficiently protects mature authority seams.
rejected_alternatives: Historical six-module map — repaired principles are useful, but the Judging Operations/Evaluation seam is now unnecessarily high-coupling.
Broad monolith/package topology — lower structural cost but insufficient protection against cross-owner mutation and derived-authority leakage.
Selective services — no demonstrated driver justifies network consistency, retry and operational complexity yet.
decisions.reversibility_migration: Moderately reversible while still in one application boundary. No network protocol, database-per-module or package layout is selected. Future service extraction remains possible through preserved public contracts, but moving semantic ownership requires explicit architecture governance.
residual_uncertainty: exact transaction boundaries for coordinated cross-module actions
whether any module later requires an independent runtime process
revisit_triggers: module requires materially independent scale/isolation/availability/runtime
ordinary workflows are dominated by expensive cross-module coordination

decisions.title: Authoritative Persistence, History, Provenance & Projection Architecture
decisions.selected_option: One logical PostgreSQL-compatible relational authority store with explicit append-stable semantic history and authority-first recovery (PST-001..PST-016)
alternatives_evaluated: PostgreSQL-compatible relational current state plus explicit append-stable semantic history
scenario_seeds: affected Outcome Declaration with same visible winner
decisions.rationale: A PostgreSQL-compatible relational authority store best fits stable identity, constrained current state, transactional integrity and the accepted modular-monolith boundary while explicit immutable Version/Provenance history preserves current-versus-historical truth without imposing system-wide event sourcing. Projections remain secondary and rebuildable; migrations and restore are authority/history preserving.
rejected_alternatives: Historical PostgreSQL/RDS design unchanged — persistence-family reasoning is useful but RDS/Multi-AZ and old module topology belong to later/current decisions.
Provider-neutral relational/hybrid — too underspecified for later implementation planning; PostgreSQL-family coupling is acceptable and explicit.
System-wide event sourcing — stronger operational/query complexity than current semantic/history obligations require.
decisions.reversibility_migration: Intentional PostgreSQL-family coupling with one logical authority database. Stable application IDs, module-owned contracts, additive migrations and no managed-service selection preserve future migration/extraction paths. Moving to a different engine would require data/schema migration but not semantic redesign if PST contracts are preserved.
revisit_triggers: required scale/access pattern cannot be met proportionately by relational authority storage
justified service extraction requires independent module storage
binding retention/legal obligation conflicts with immutable-history posture
temporal/audit requirements make log reconstruction materially superior
selected concurrency/transaction architecture cannot preserve current/history semantics
required recovery targets cannot be met by accepted storage model
whole-architecture validation exposes unacceptable persistence, migration or recovery risk

decisions.title: Identity, Authentication, Participation, Access & Session Architecture
decisions.selected_option: Managed standards-compatible external authentication behind an application adapter, stable MUDAC Identity/Participation/Access, and opaque first-party server session (IAM-001..IAM-018)
alternatives_evaluated: Self-hosted MUDAC credentials and authentication protocols
Managed external IdP with browser/provider bearer-session authority
Managed standards-compatible external IdP plus MUDAC-owned Identity/Participation/Access and first-party opaque server session
decisions.rationale: MUDAC requires stable human identity continuity without transferring Competition authority to authentication infrastructure. A managed standards-compatible external IdP behind an adapter plus MUDAC-owned Identity, Competition-scoped Participation, contextual Access and opaque first-party server sessions preserves authority separation, supports shared-device/revocation behavior and minimizes provider lock-in.
rejected_alternatives: Historical candidate unchanged — provider-independent semantics are strong, but historical provider/runtime assumptions require fresh selection.
Provider-native roles/groups/claims — collapses authentication/provider administration into contextual Competition authority.
Self-hosted credentials — materially higher credential-security/operational burden without current product need.
Browser/provider bearer-session authority — increases stale-claim/browser-token exposure and weakens application revocation/currentness.
decisions.reversibility_migration: Provider lock-in is intentionally bounded: MUDAC Identity IDs, Participation/Access and application session semantics remain application-owned. Provider replacement requires account-link/reverification and session migration but not rewriting Competition authority or authorship history.
revisit_triggers: concrete provider cannot preserve stable MUDAC Identity/application-owned Access
shared-device operation cannot be made safe with selected session model
required federation/SSO changes application/provider authority boundary
session availability/revocation needs cannot be met proportionately
legal/security requirements change authentication assurance or retention expectations
whole-architecture validation exposes privilege, stale-access or operator-authority leakage

decisions.title: Application Interface, Command/Query, Transaction, Concurrency, Retry & Idempotency Architecture
decisions.selected_option: Versioned HTTPS/JSON explicit command-query boundary with synchronous commit-confirmed authority, optimistic concurrency, durable logical-operation idempotency, narrow atomic coordination and truthful reconciliation (CMD-001..CMD-022)
alternatives_evaluated: Explicit synchronous command/query contracts with optimistic concurrency and durable idempotency
scenario_seeds: lost-response retry after consequential authoritative action
decisions.rationale: The accepted modular monolith and one logical authority database allow ordinary owner-local transactions plus a few semantically indivisible cross-module atomic transitions. Explicit command/query contracts preserve high-consequence intent, optimistic current-state checks prevent stale overwrite, durable operation identity converges retries, and domain uniqueness remains the final backstop. Queue-first processing and global strong locking add complexity not justified by the bounded live-event workload.
rejected_alternatives: Historical candidate unchanged — strong ideas but stale outcome binding and inherited isolation/runtime choices require revalidation.
Broad CRUD/resource mutation — obscures consequential semantic actions and weakens retry/currentness modeling.
Queue/job-first commands — makes ordinary event-day authority unnecessarily indirect and risks conflating accepted work with semantic success.
Global strongest locking/isolation — excessive contention/complexity and still does not solve lost-response or idempotency semantics.
decisions.reversibility_migration: Intentional commitment to HTTPS/JSON baseline command-query contracts, optimistic concurrency and durable operation identity. Internal framework, ORM, route layout, revision encoding, DB isolation and queue technology remain unselected. Future service extraction requires redesign of narrow cross-module atomic seams but can preserve the public command semantics.
residual_uncertainty: exact PostgreSQL locking/isolation choices per command
exact asynchronous operation storage/queue where needed
exact pagination strategy per query family
revisit_triggers: browser/API workload needs a different baseline transport family
cross-module atomic seams become incompatible with justified service extraction
contention makes optimistic concurrency materially inadequate
long-running authoritative work requires broader asynchronous semantics
durable idempotency retention creates unacceptable cost/privacy constraints
whole-architecture validation finds unsafe retry, ambiguity, partial-result or transaction behavior

decisions.title: Offline Draft, Multi-device, Degraded & Paper Recovery Architecture
decisions.selected_option: Server-authoritative Draft currentness with bounded non-authoritative local continuity, revision-aware reconnect, explicit conflict preservation, one-logical-Scorecard multi-device convergence, no disconnected authority, privacy-safe shared-device recovery, and paper/electronic reconciliation (RCV-001..RCV-018)
alternatives_evaluated: Repaired historical Synchronization/Offline Recovery candidate unchanged
Online-only digital operation with paper fallback
General local-first / CRDT-style offline application authority
Durable offline command outbox with automatic replay of all intent
Bounded non-authoritative local Draft continuity with server-authoritative reconciliation and paper fallback
decisions.rationale: Current semantics require continuity without independent device/paper authority. Bounded local Draft persistence reduces transient work loss while server-owned currentness, current IAM revalidation, CMD revision/idempotency/reconciliation, explicit conflict preservation and one-logical-Scorecard uniqueness prevent offline or multi-device traces from multiplying authority. Paper remains an alternate capture/source channel with the same basis, authorship and weight.
rejected_alternatives: Historical candidate unchanged — useful continuity semantics but stale Encounter binding and inherited client/runtime mechanisms require current re-establishment.
Online-only digital operation — smallest client state but unnecessarily loses recoverable Judge work during transient connectivity failures.
General local-first/CRDT authority — current Access, basis, Finalization and evaluation meaning are not generally safe to merge offline.
Blind durable command outbox — consequential intent can become stale/unauthorized and would create a second command-authority model beside CMD reconciliation.
decisions.reversibility_migration: Commits to server-authoritative Draft currentness, bounded local non-authoritative continuity, revision-aware reconciliation, no general offline authority and one-logical-evaluation convergence. Browser storage, encryption, autosave, service worker/background sync, queue/runtime and exact retention remain unselected for later ADQ-008/ADQ-009/implementation decisions.
residual_uncertainty: whether background retry materially improves experience
safe automatic-merge field classes, if any
revisit_triggers: event operation requires general disconnected authority rather than bounded Draft continuity
browser/platform constraints cannot preserve continuity/privacy safely
measured multi-device conflict frequency makes explicit reconciliation operationally unacceptable
local continuity retention creates unacceptable privacy/compliance risk
paper fallback cannot preserve required basis/provenance at event scale
service extraction invalidates current command/current-state reconciliation assumptions
whole-architecture validation exposes unresolved duplication, stale-authority or degraded-operation risk

decisions.title: Artifact, Export, Publication & External Delivery Architecture
decisions.selected_option: Exact-source Export records with immutable integrity-addressed Artifact bytes behind authoritative relational metadata, complete-surface disclosure validation, explicit Publication, successor replacement, truthful withdrawal and non-authoritative delivery (ART-001..ART-020)
alternatives_evaluated: Large durable binary payloads inside relational authority storage
Immutable durable artifacts behind authoritative relational metadata with explicit Publication
scenario_seeds: withdrawn Publication while external copies remain
decisions.rationale: Current Export/Publication semantics require exact historical source basis, separate representation currency and distribution authority, reconstructible provenance, explicit successor release and truthful withdrawal limits. Relational semantic metadata plus immutable object/blob bytes preserves these obligations without burdening transactional authority storage with large payloads or selecting ADQ-009 runtime/provider mechanisms.
rejected_alternatives: Historical candidate unchanged — useful semantics but stale Encounter-era wording and inherited AWS/S3/CloudFront/SQS selections.
Transient generation only — cannot reliably reconstruct the exact durable representation previously printed/released after source/renderer/template evolution.
Mutable latest artifact — silently rewrites historical byte identity and retargets prior release.
Large binary payloads in authority DB — couples transactional backup/recovery to large immutable files without semantic benefit.
decisions.reversibility_migration: Commits to durable Export identity, immutable retained Artifact bytes with integrity identity, relational semantic metadata, an object/blob boundary for large bytes, explicit Publication, successor replacement and delivery non-authority. Object-store vendor, CDN, renderer, queue, print/email providers, signed-link mechanism and exact retention remain unselected.
residual_uncertainty: exact object/blob storage service and durability tier
revisit_triggers: representation formats cannot preserve source/disclosure fidelity
provider/runtime constraints make immutable identity or controlled withdrawal infeasible
retained-artifact storage cost becomes disproportionate
binding retention/erasure law conflicts with retained-history semantics
delivery integrations require independent authoritative workflow semantics
whole-architecture validation exposes unresolved disclosure, stale-copy, successor or release-history risk

decisions.title: Browser/Client State, Navigation, Accessibility & Degraded Interaction Architecture
decisions.selected_option: Framework-neutral client-rich browser architecture subordinate to server authority, with explicit remote-cache/command/local-Draft/context/ephemeral state partitioning, context-safe navigation, phone-primary Judge workflows, responsive Organizer density, accessibility semantic parity, explicit degraded/conflict/unknown recovery, and replaceable client mechanisms (CLT-001..CLT-020)
alternatives_evaluated: Repaired historical FE architecture including React/Router/Query/IndexedDB selections
Minimal server-rendered/progressively enhanced browser with very limited client state
General local-first browser architecture with offline authority and broad merge
Thin browser around a framework-specific server-driven interaction platform
Framework-neutral client-rich browser with explicit server authority and state partitioning
decisions.rationale: Current Phase-013 Experience and accepted IAM/CMD/RCV authority justify rich browser interaction for interruption-resistant judging, local Draft continuity, conflict/unknown recovery, phone-primary Judge work, dense Organizer live operations and accessibility parity, but do not justify browser semantic authority or premature package/framework selection.
rejected_alternatives: Historical FE stack unchanged — interaction principles remain useful, but React/Router/Query/IndexedDB require fresh technology revalidation and exact router/query packages are explicitly deferred.
Minimal server-rendered/progressive enhancement — simpler client state but weaker fit for bounded Draft continuity, live-event interruption recovery, rich conflict handling and dense live operations.
General local-first browser authority — conflicts with RCV current Access, no-offline-authority and safe reconciliation semantics.
Framework-specific server-driven baseline — still requires client Draft/recovery state and introduces unnecessary framework coupling without current evidence.
decisions.reversibility_migration: Commits to a client-rich browser interaction class, explicit client state partitions, server-authoritative semantics, context/private-state isolation, bounded RCV local Draft continuity, explicit uncertainty/recovery, phone-primary Judge completion and accessibility semantic parity. React, TypeScript, router/query/storage/state/component/build/push/test tooling remain implementation selections.
residual_uncertainty: whether existing React/TypeScript substrate should be retained
revisit_triggers: client-rich state complexity exceeds its live-event/offline value
a server-rendered/progressively enhanced approach materially simplifies implementation without degrading RCV or Experience obligations
browser storage/security constraints cannot preserve shared-device privacy
target-device/browser support cannot meet semantic accessibility/degraded requirements
measured client performance makes current partitioning disproportionate
whole-architecture validation exposes unresolved state-leakage, accessibility, degraded-mode or recovery risk
